claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by rapid, high-energy input rather than by the specific synthesis technique.
Rapid, high-energy input causes all metal species to nucleate and mix simultaneously.
Simultaneous nucleation and mixing occur before diffusion-driven segregation can take place.
A concentrated energy burst provides nearly instantaneous thermal activation for nucleation and atomic mixing.
An inert or reducing atmosphere prevents oxidation during synthesis.
A transient high-temperature state induces rapid nucleation.
Limiting the time available for atomic diffusion suppresses phase separation.
Rapid processing preserves high surface-atom exposure.
Fast, concentrated energy input bypasses thermodynamically preferred phase separation.
Under slower energy input, differences in atomic mobility cause elemental segregation and distinct phases or other inhomogeneities.
Relative to gradual energy delivery, a concentrated energy burst will produce nanoparticles with a more uniform distribution of all constituent elements.
Relative to gradual energy delivery, a concentrated energy burst will produce a larger surface area of well-mixed noble metals.
Relative to gradual energy delivery, a concentrated energy burst will reduce elemental segregation.
The proposed mechanism should apply when constituent metals have relatively similar diffusion rates and melting points.
Many noble metals have relatively similar diffusion rates and melting points.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when constituent metals have drastically different diffusivities.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when post-synthesis annealing dominates microstructure development.
Available comparative outcomes suggest that energy-delivery rate is critical.

contradictions.description: Atomic mixing is attributed to thermally activated motion, while segregation is said to be suppressed by limiting atomic diffusion; the hypothesis does not explain how sufficient transport for mixing occurs without also enabling segregation.
